title: Only, Just & Lists: ばかり, しか, だけで, でも, し, たり, とか
description: Nothing but (ばかり), only (しか〜ない), just by (だけで), or something (でも), reasons and examples (し, など, たり〜たり, とか〜とか).

points.title: 〜ばかり: nothing but, only (too much)
points.summary: Noun + ばかり / て-form + ばかりいる = 'nothing but …' — usually with a critical tone.
points.body:
- 弟は漫画**ばかり**読んでいる (my brother reads nothing but manga).
- 彼は寝て**ばかり**いる (he does nothing but sleep).

Particles が/を usually disappear before ばかり; others stay: 友達と**ばかり**遊ぶ.

Don't confuse with **た-form + ばかり** = 'just did' (来たばかり).
examples: {弟|おとうと}は{漫画|まんが}ばかり{読|よ}んでいます。
My brother reads nothing but manga.
{彼|かれ}は{毎日|まいにち}{寝|ね}てばかりいます。
He does nothing but sleep every day.

points.title: 〜しか〜ない: only (not more than)
points.summary: Noun / quantity + しか + NEGATIVE verb = only. Stresses that it's not enough. Never with a positive verb.
points.body:
- 財布に100円**しかありません** (I only have 100 yen).
- 日本語は少し**しか**話せ**ません**.

**Always negative:** ✗ 100円しかあります.

**しか vs だけ:** だけ is neutral and goes with positive verbs (100円だけあります); しか + negative stresses shortage.
examples: {財布|さいふ}に100{円|えん}しかありません。
I only have 100 yen in my wallet.
{日本語|にほんご}は{少|すこ}ししか{話|はな}せません。
I can only speak a little Japanese.

points.title: 〜だけで: just by, merely by
points.summary: Verb (dictionary) / noun + だけで = just by (doing), with just … (a big result from a small thing).
points.body:
- このボタンを押す**だけで**、電気がつきます (just by pressing this button…).
- 彼女の声を聞く**だけで**元気になる.
- 一人**だけで**行きました (went alone, with just one person).

It highlights that very little is needed.
examples: このボタンを{押|お}すだけで、{電気|でんき}がつきます。
Just pressing this button turns on the light.
{彼女|かのじょ}の{声|こえ}を{聞|き}くだけで、{元気|げんき}になります。
Just hearing her voice cheers me up.

points.title: 〜でも: … or something
points.summary: Noun + でも softens an invitation or suggestion: 'tea or something'. It replaces が/を.
points.body:
- お茶**でも**飲みませんか (how about some tea or something?).
- 映画**でも**見に行こうか.

It keeps the suggestion light and leaves room for alternatives. Particles が/を disappear: ✗ お茶をでも.

(Other uses: question word + でも = any (何でも, いつでも); 〜ても / でも = even if.)
examples: {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}きましたね。お{茶|ちゃ}でも{飲|の}みませんか。
I'm thirsty — shall we have some tea or something?
{週末|しゅうまつ}、{映画|えいが}でも{見|み}に{行|い}こうか。
Shall we go see a movie or something this weekend?

points.title: 〜など: such as, and so on
points.summary: Noun (や noun) + など = examples from a larger set. More formal than とか.
points.body:
- 京都や奈良**など**に行きました.
- 冷蔵庫に卵や牛乳**など**があります.

Often paired with や: AやB**など**. Particles follow など: など**に**, など**を**, など**が**.

Casual: なんか / とか.
examples: {京都|きょうと}や{奈良|なら}などに{行|い}きました。
I went to places like Kyoto and Nara.
{冷蔵庫|れいぞうこ}に{卵|たまご}や{牛乳|ぎゅうにゅう}などがあります。
There are eggs, milk and so on in the fridge.

points.title: 〜し、〜し: and (what's more) — listing reasons
points.summary: Plain form + し lists reasons or features: 'it's cheap, and it's tasty, (so…)'. Nouns / な-adj take だ: 静かだし.
points.body:
- この店は安い**し**、おいしい**し**、よく来ます.
- 雨だ**し**、寒い**し**、今日は家にいよう.

**Attachment:** plain form; nouns and な-adjectives need **だ**: 学生**だし**, 静か**だし** (✗ 静かなし).

Often only one し is said, implying more reasons: もう遅い**し**、帰ろう.
examples: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}いし、おいしいし、よく{来|き}ます。
This shop is cheap and tasty, so I come often.
{部屋|へや}が{静|しず}かだし、{駅|えき}にも{近|ちか}いです。
The room is quiet, and it's close to the station too.

points.title: 〜たり〜たりする: do things like A and B
points.summary: た-form + り, た-form + り + する = listing example actions (not all, not in order). Must end with する.
points.body:
- 休みの日は本を読ん**だり**、音楽を聞い**たり**します.

**Formation:** take the た-form and add り: 読んだ → 読ん**だり**, 聞いた → 聞い**たり**, 行った → 行っ**たり**.
The list must end with **する** (します, した, したい …).

Also for alternating states: 降っ**たり**止んだり (on and off).
examples: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{本|ほん}を{読|よ}んだり、{音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}いたりします。
On days off I do things like read and listen to music.
{週末|しゅうまつ}は{掃除|そうじ}をしたり{洗濯|せんたく}をしたりしました。
On the weekend I did things like cleaning and laundry.

points.title: 〜とか〜とか: things like (casual)
points.summary: Noun/verb + とか, noun/verb + とか = casual listing of examples. Equivalent to や〜など / たり〜たり in speech.
points.body:
- 寿司**とか**天ぷら**とか**が好きです.
- 映画を見る**とか**、買い物する**とか**.

It can list nouns *and* actions. Casual — in writing use や〜など.
examples: {日本料理|にほんりょうり}では{寿司|すし}とか{天|てん}ぷらとかが{好|す}きです。
Of Japanese food, I like things like sushi and tempura.

questions.prompt: {弟|おとうと}は{勉強|べんきょう}しないで、{漫画|まんが}（　）{読|よ}んでいます。
notes: だけで = 'just by' — doesn't fit.
ほど = 'extent' — doesn't fit.
しか needs a negative verb.
questions.translation: My brother doesn't study — he reads nothing but manga.

questions.prompt: {彼|かれ}は{毎日|まいにち}{寝|ね}て（　）います。
questions.explanation: て-form + **ばかりいる** = does nothing but.
notes: しか needs a negative verb.
ずつ means 'each'.
寝てだけでいます isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: He does nothing but sleep every day.

questions.prompt: {財布|さいふ}に100{円|えん}（　）ありません。
notes: ばかり + ありません doesn't make 'only'.
100円だけありません = 'it's not just 100 yen that's missing' — wrong meaning.
100円まであります/ありません doesn't express 'only' — まで means 'up to'.
questions.translation: I only have 100 yen in my wallet.

questions.prompt: {日本語|にほんご}は{少|すこ}ししか（　）。
questions.explanation: しか always needs a **negative** verb.
notes: Positive — ungrammatical with しか.
Positive past — ungrammatical with しか.
しか + positive is ungrammatical.
questions.translation: I can only speak a little Japanese.

questions.prompt: このボタンを{押|お}す（　）、{電気|でんき}がつきます。
notes: しか needs a negative verb.
だけを can't follow a verb this way.
だけに means 'precisely because' (N2) — not 'just by'.
questions.translation: Just pressing this button turns on the light.

questions.prompt: {彼女|かのじょ}の{声|こえ}を{聞|き}く（　）{元気|げんき}になります。
notes: 聞くばかりで isn't natural here.
だけに = 'precisely because' — different meaning.
しかで isn't grammatical.
questions.translation: Just hearing her voice cheers me up.

questions.prompt: {喉|のど}が{渇|かわ}きましたね。お{茶|ちゃ}（　）{飲|の}みませんか。
notes: ばかり = 'nothing but'.
しか needs a negative and means 'only'.
だけ = 'only' — not a soft invitation.
questions.translation: I'm thirsty — shall we have some tea or something?

questions.prompt: {週末|しゅうまつ}、{映画|えいが}（　）{見|み}に{行|い}こうか。
questions.explanation: **でも** replaces を: 映画でも見に行こう.
notes: でが isn't a combination.
映画では = 'as for movies / in movies' — not a suggestion.
でを isn't a combination.
questions.translation: Shall we go see a movie or something this weekend?

questions.prompt: {夏休|なつやす}みは{京都|きょうと}や{奈良|なら}（　）に{行|い}きました。
questions.explanation: AやB**など** = places like A and B.
notes: しか needs a negative verb (しか{行|い}きませんでした) and can't take に like this.
なんど means 'how many times'.
まで = 'until/as far as'.
questions.translation: Over summer vacation I went to places like Kyoto and Nara.

questions.prompt: この{店|みせ}は{安|やす}い（　）、おいしいし、よく{来|き}ます。
notes: たり attaches to the た-form ({安|やす}かったり) and comes in pairs.
安いが = 'cheap, but…' — contradicts the second positive reason.
い-adjectives connect with くて, not て.
questions.translation: This shop is cheap and tasty, so I come often.

questions.prompt: {部屋|へや}が{静|しず}か（　）し、{駅|えき}にも{近|ちか}いです。
notes: な can't come before し.
でし isn't a form.
のし isn't a form.
questions.translation: The room is quiet, and it's close to the station too.

questions.prompt: {休|やす}みの{日|ひ}は{本|ほん}を{読|よ}ん（　）、{音楽|おんがく}を{聞|き}いたりします。
questions.explanation: 読む → 読んだ → **読んだり**.
notes: 読む's past ends in だ, so たり becomes だり.
読んで is the て-form — the list needs たり/だり.
でり isn't a form.
questions.translation: On days off I do things like read and listen to music.

questions.prompt: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{掃除|そうじ}をしたり{洗濯|せんたく}をしたり（　）。
questions.explanation: The たり-list must end with **する** (here: しました).
notes: しりました isn't a form.
ました needs a stem.
でした can't close a たり-list of actions.
questions.translation: On the weekend I did things like cleaning and laundry.

questions.prompt: {日本料理|にほんりょうり}では、{寿司|すし}（　）{天|てん}ぷら（　）が{好|す}きです。
questions.explanation: Casual list of examples: **AとかBとか**.
notes: と…とか mixes two patterns.
しか needs a negative verb.
とか…や mixes two patterns.
questions.translation: Of Japanese food, I like things like sushi and tempura.
